findings.reason: the section would sit unbuilt indefinitely with the plan's own chain reading complete, which is the same defect the earlier reviews raised against f-wftl-011 and f-wftl-012.
findings.text: §42 is declared implementable (plan.html:23, plan.html:229) and is named by no followup: f-wftl-013, the plan's only open followup, names §22 and §9 only, so a coordinator driving the plan from its open followup with its recommended invocation (/reckon-build work-flows-to-the-lane §22) never dispatches §42

findings.reason: a node reading "no command performs it" will build a second extractor beside a working one the section itself relies on ("the figure the routing derivation computes"), instead of delivering the residual gap (a dry run by default and a report across every project in the shared crew home).
findings.text: the Why states the other projects' rows "were never backfilled, and no command performs it", but scripts/derive_run_figures.py (committed at 1d7f6bcd06 on 2026-09-09, before this section was written) is a re-runnable, idempotent command that takes --project and --root, fills tool_steps and orientation_input_tokens from the run's own stream, records both as absent (never zero) when the stream is gone, and reports rows filled and rows skipped per project — so the stated gap is wider than the system's actual state

findings.reason: absence is the destructive outcome the section introduces, and without a bound on it the live gate cannot fail on exactly the implementation that loses the evidence the section exists to preserve.
findings.text: the applied-run gate requires only that a retention dry run from a fresh cursor report a missing-derived-figure count of zero, and no case bounds how many rows the command records as absent: a command that wrongly resolves every stream as gone records absence on all 2,614 rows, which retention treats as reapable, so the streams are destroyed and the gate still passes — and the dry-run case ("reports a fill count per project") passes on an all-zero count
